nodes.description: Prolonged multidrug antimycobacterial treatment is selected by organism and susceptibility. Reported combinations include rifampicin, isoniazid, ethambutol and macrolides, with levofloxacin in refractory BCG disease. One severe MAC case received azithromycin, linezolid, moxifloxacin and bedaquiline. The report documents bedaquiline discontinuation after QT prolongation and subsequent clofazimine addition, but later again lists bedaquiline in the current regimen; any restart timing is not established. These are case-specific regimens, not a single standard combination for every pathogen.

nodes.description: Adjunctive recombinant IFN-gamma has been used with antimycobacterial therapy in refractory dominant partial deficiency, where residual receptor signaling remains. Administration supplements signaling; it does not replace the defective receptor.

nodes.description: Reduced circulating myeloid and plasmacytoid dendritic-cell counts occurred in two patients with active infection; the index patient also had lymph-node pDC depletion. Counts normalized after treatment and were normal in an infection-free comparator with the same genetic disorder. This small series supports an infection-associated observation, not a constitutive developmental defect or an established population frequency.
